name: schema-form
purpose: Renders a complete form from a JSON Schema subset (draft 2020-12 keywords) and an optional UI schema, with the existing AbsoluteUI controls inside a native form managed by Form. Controls are named by JSON Pointer, so values validate, serialize, and show the Error Summary exactly like a hand-written form; getValue() returns typed JSON, aui-submit carries the validated value, and server errors map back with setErrors(pointer -> message). Unsupported keywords are configuration errors, never silently ignored.
whenToUse: Forms defined by configuration or by administrators (questionnaires, request types, settings pages).
Many similar forms whose fields change without a release.
whenNotToUse: A single, stable form with custom layout or behavior: compose Form, Form Field, and the controls directly.
Schemas that need $ref, allOf/anyOf, if/then/else, or arbitrary oneOf subschemas (not supported).
Spreadsheet-like data entry: use Data Grid.
responsive: Fields flow in one column; a UI schema `columns` value (1 to 4) applies as far as the form's container allows: about 13rem per column (2 columns from 27rem, 3 from 41rem, 4 from 55rem; container queries), one column below 27rem, so narrow screens never scroll horizontally. Array item actions wrap under the item.
rtl: Layout uses logical properties; the controls mirror as they do on their own. JSON Pointers and values are direction-neutral.
theme: Uses the global tokens only (spacing, border, radius, text colors) and the themes of the controls it renders; groups and arrays have a border that becomes CanvasText in forced colors.
timezone: Date fields emit ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD), date-time fields ISO instants in UTC (toISOString), time fields HH:MM:SS. Date-time fields use the `timezone` option or the global configuration. With a business calendar, `disableNonWorking` in the UI schema blocks weekends and holidays.
security: Labels, help text, and options are rendered as text. Rich-text fields are sanitized by Rich Text Editor. Conditions are plain JSON evaluated by a fixed interpreter: no eval or Function. Patterns compile with the u flag and are limited to 500 characters; schemas are limited in depth (8) and size (500 fields).
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry; the async validator and submission handling belong to the application.

performance.testedScale: Up to 500 fields and arrays of 100 entries; every field is a real control in the DOM (no virtualization).

limitations: Conditions compare values with equals, notEquals, in, and filled, combined with all, any, and not.
Arrays of arrays are not supported; array items are primitives or objects.
Reordering array entries rebuilds their controls (focus moves to the corresponding action button).
unsupported: $ref, $defs, allOf, anyOf, not, if/then/else, dependentSchemas, patternProperties, and type arrays.
Formats other than date, date-time, time, email, and uri.
Custom widgets (use Form with your own controls).
antiPatterns: Generating a schema per user at runtime to work around missing conditions: keep one schema and use visibleIf.
Hiding required information behind conditions that the user cannot discover.
